title: Week 2 Fantasy Football Inactives: Collins Out, Flowers Doubtful, Burrow Questionable for Sunday Playoff Push
body:
The NFL’s Week 2 slate is shaping up to be a roller‑coaster for fantasy owners, with several high‑profile players listed as inactive, doubtful or only questionable for Sunday’s games. The most consequential blow comes from the Buffalo Bills, who have officially ruled wide receiver Marquez Collins out of action after a lingering ankle injury. Meanwhile, the New York Jets’ rookie wideout Garrett Flowers is listed as doubtful, and Cincinnati’s quarterback Joe Burrow remains a question mark after a minor shoulder tweak in practice. These developments force managers to scramble for viable replacements and re‑evaluate lineups that could be the difference between a win and a loss in their leagues.

Collins’ absence is a significant hit for the Bills’ offense and for fantasy managers who have been banking on his explosive playmaking ability. The 6‑foot‑3 receiver has logged 79 receiving yards and a touchdown in his first two games, making him a popular flex option for many teams. With him sidelined, Buffalo will likely lean more heavily on Stefon Diggs and the emerging duo of Gabe Davis and James Cook. For fantasy owners, the safest play is to bench Collins and pivot to Diggs as the primary WR1, while keeping an eye on Davis, who has been targeted consistently in the red zone and could provide a solid floor in a flex slot.

Garrett Flowers’ doubtful status adds another layer of uncertainty for the Jets’ backfield. The 22‑year‑old rookie has shown flashes of big‑play potential, but his production has been limited to a handful of catches and a single rushing attempt so far. If the Jets decide to keep him on the sideline, the fantasy upside shifts to veteran wideout Garrett Wilson and the newly acquired veteran receiver Mike Williams, both of whom have higher usage rates. Managers who have been slotting Flowers in a flex or bench role should consider moving him to the bench and promoting Wilson, who has already posted 45 receiving yards and a touchdown in the first two weeks.

Joe Burrow’s situation is perhaps the most nuanced of the three. The Cincinnati quarterback suffered a minor shoulder strain during a pre‑game warm‑up but is listed as questionable rather than out. The Bengals have not announced a definitive status, leaving fantasy owners in a dilemma. Burrow has been a reliable source of points, averaging 22.5 fantasy points per game, and his connection with Ja’Marr Chase remains one of the league’s most potent. If Burrow is cleared to play, managers should retain him as a starter; however, a backup quarterback like Tyler Bishop or rookie Dorian Thompson could see limited snaps if Burrow is held out, offering minimal upside. In the meantime, it may be prudent to keep Burrow on the bench and monitor the official injury report up to kickoff, while loading the roster with high‑volume RBs such as Austin Ekeler and Christian McCaffrey to hedge against a potential quarterback shortfall.

Beyond the headline injuries, Week 2 presents a host of matchup‑driven decisions. The Dallas Cowboys face a struggling Detroit defense, making Dak Prescott a solid starter despite his modest 12.8 fantasy points per game average. Conversely, the New England Patriots’ secondary has tightened up, suggesting a cautious approach to starting rookie receiver Jahan Dotson against them. Tight ends also deserve attention; Dallas’ Dalton Kincaid has emerged as a reliable red‑zone target, while the Los Angeles Chargers’ Gerald Everett could see a boost against a vulnerable Seattle secondary.

Looking ahead, the injury reports for Collins, Flowers and Burrow underscore the volatile nature of fantasy football early in the season. Managers who stay agile—monitoring official updates, leveraging depth charts, and making data‑driven waiver wire pickups—will be better positioned to capitalize on emerging opportunities. As the league heads into the mid‑season stretch, the ability to adapt to sudden roster changes will separate championship contenders from the rest of the pack. Keep a close eye on the final injury reports Friday night, and be ready to adjust your lineups before the first snap on Sunday.
